Title:
Read Deep, Write Shallow: How Looped Language Models Should Spend Their Depth

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
12 pages, 6 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers several times per token and spend the same number of loops reading the prompt and writing the answer. We show that the two buy different things: depth spent reading the prompt mainly buys knowledge and long-context accuracy, while depth spent writing the answer mainly buys multi-step derivation. A small connector trained on a frozen looped model lets the prompt be read with p loops and the answer written with d loops; one set of parameters serves all 16 pairs up to four loops, and a key map that commutes with rotary embeddings lets one stored prompt KV cache serve every writing loop exactly. Reading deep and writing shallow follows: on Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, reading four loops and writing two scores higher than the native two-loop model on all eight standard benchmarks we test, at the same decode depth, and comes within two points of the native four-loop model on six of them while answering GSM8K in 0.55x its time. With the writer fixed, reading deeper improves knowledge and long-context benchmarks on five checkpoints from two model families. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow
